metadata.title: Stock market today: S&P 500, Nasdaq waver after Nvidia clears hurdle, Anthropic prepares to price its IPO

content.text:
US stocks wobbled on Wednesday after a turbulent start to the week as Nvidia (NVDA) cleared its earnings bar and investors awaited the next big AI catalyst: Anthropic's (ANTH.PVT) IPO.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) fell 0.3%. The S&P 500 (^GSPC) erased early trading gains to slip into red territory, while the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) hovered near the flatline following two straight days of declines.
Markets wavered somewhat after Nvidia reported its first earnings since Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO, demonstrating that the AI chip king can continue to deliver a quarter as good as any, even with a scandal overhang. Revenue surged 103% year over year, and the board said it would not reinstate Huang.
Nvidia stock rose in early Wednesday trading but trimmed gains following a four-day losing streak. Other semiconductor stocks, such as AMD (AMD), also lost steam in early trading.
7,360.62 +20.09 (+0.27%)
As of 10:00:17 AM EST. Market Open.
Anthropic is expected to price its initial public offering this evening, initiating what is expected to be one of the largest public debuts in markets on Thursday. Here's everything you need to know ahead of Anthropic's IPO.
On the earnings calendar, Target (TGT) quarterly results smashed expectations, while Home Depot's counterpart, Lowe's (LOW), also beat Wall Street estimates on Wednesday. On the economic front, the Federal Reserve will release the minutes of its October meeting, and housing indicators will tell us whether the real estate market remains frozen.
LIVE 6 updates
Tech stocks look to stage a comeback after Nvidia earnings
US stocks opened slightly higher Wednesday, with the spotlight focused firmly on Wall Street and this week's two biggest tests for the artificial intelligence trade.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) fell 0.4%. The S&P 500 (^GSPC) rose 0.2%, and those on the Nasdaq-100 (^IXIC) gained 0.7%.
Investors are digesting Nvidia's first earnings report since Jensen Huang's departure. They are also waiting for Anthropic to share the final pricing for its marquee initial public offering, which is expected to begin trading sometime Thursday.
50,511.40 -248.02 (-0.49%)
As of 10:00:17 AM EST. Market Open.
Target (TGT), TJX Companies (TJX), and Home Depot rival Lowe's (LOW) reported earnings Wednesday. The Federal Reserve will also release the minutes of its October meeting.
Into Wednesday's open, oil prices declined further, with the benchmark Brent Crude futures (BZ=F) now hovering below $90 per barrel, its lowest level since late August.
BlackRock makes bigger Brazil bet with $17 billion asset manager deal.
BlackRock (BLK) shares rose in Wednesday premarket trading after the world's largest asset manager said it's clinching a bigger bet on Brazil's growing investment industry.
The world's largest asset manager said Wednesday it agreed to acquire SulAmérica Investimentos, a Brazilian money manager that oversees roughly $17 billion of investor dollars.
BlackRock has operated in Brazil since 2008, but said the acquisition will give it a broader local platform spanning fixed income, private credit, equities and multi-asset strategies. SulAmérica has more than 25 distribution agreements across Brazil's wealth industry and relationships with roughly 200 pension funds.
The bet comes as Brazil's asset-management industry continues to expand. The country has roughly $2 trillion in managed assets today, according to BlackRock, which cited estimates that the figure could reach $3 trillion by 2030 as fee-based advice and ETF adoption grow.
The deal also comes weeks after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's surprise election victory that initially rattled Brazilian markets.
Target earnings squash estimates as inflation-weary shoppers see great deals
Target (TGT) shares are moving lower in premarket trading despite earnings smashing expectations. Target CEO Michael Fiddelke told Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi that the retailer's strong results are because of a better shopping experience and lower prices.
"At the start of the year we were laser focused on what our strategy needed to be, and it's getting back to the unique lane that we play in retail, and that's always going to be a combination of leading with style and design, and of course, incredible value," Fiddelke told Sozzi. "The 'I can't believe the quality of this,' or 'I can't believe I found it at Target at a price point' that makes the smile get wider."
Here's what Target reported in the third quarter:
-
Net sales: +7.1% year over year to $27.1 billion versus estimates of $26.5 billion.
-
Diluted earnings per share: +49% year over year to $2.65 versus estimates of $2.08.
-
Comparable sales: +5.6% year over year versus +3.61% estimate (last-year comparable sales fell 2.7%).
-
Digital comparable sales: +9.8%
-
Store comparable sales: +4.6%
Read more about Target's earnings.
The 'low hire, low fire' job market could finally crack in 2027
Yahoo Finance's Kerry Hannon outlines the top three trends to watch, according to a report from Indeed Hiring Lab and Glassdoor Economic Research. One of those top trends: Job hopping may make a comeback.
Kerry writes:
Workers' pent-up frustration over feeling stuck in their job could quickly shift. Rising job postings and upbeat hiring managers point to a rebound that could unleash turnover.
"After years of very little movement, several metros are starting to turn the corner," Laura Ullrich, director of economic research at the Indeed Hiring Lab, told Yahoo Finance. "Job postings are now above pre-pandemic levels in more than three-quarters of major metros.
"It's too early to call it a recovery, but more local markets moving in the right direction is an encouraging sign heading into 2027."
This year, the job market "kept a lot of unhappy workers right where they were," said Daniel Zhao, Glassdoor's chief economist.
Read more.
Asia stocks choppy after Nvidia earnings as Anthropic pricing looms
Reuters reports:
Stocks erased early gains in Asia on Wednesday after Nvidia posted a better-than-expected sales forecast, as investor confidence remained fragile over questions about the company's future leadership and potential impacts on its regional supply chain.
In choppy trade, MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan reversed an initial rally to be down 0.1%, narrowly extending its losing streak into a fifth day. Japan's Nikkei 225 slid 0.3%, while US S&P 500 e-mini futures clung to gains, up 0.3%.
"Nvidia's results were reassuring and gave investors a reason to refocus on earnings, but they haven't resolved the broader questions around AI spending returns, financing sustainability and leadership uncertainty," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Bank in Singapore.
"So we are seeing an initial relief rally, but not necessarily the conviction needed for a sustained recovery."
Read more.
Good morning. Here's what's happening today.

Earnings calendar: Palo Alto Networks (PANW), The TJX Companies (TJX), Lowe's Companies (LOW), Target (TGT)
